key_insight: A PEDOT:PSS/graphene/n-silicon trilayer combines improved photovoltaic performance with graphene-enabled environmental protection.
engineering_relevance: The planar architecture offers a route to more efficient, durable hybrid Schottky solar cells on untextured silicon.
method: Benchmark trilayer cells against graphene/n-Si and PEDOT:PSS/n-Si reference cells.
Use PEDOT:PSS for anti-reflection, moderate graphene p-doping, and enhanced conductivity.
Use graphene as a charge-transport interface and moisture barrier.
evidence_signal: The trilayer achieved 8.52% efficiency versus 4.56% for graphene/n-Si and retained approximately 90% of its initial efficiency after 75 days in ambient conditions, versus approximately 29% for PEDOT:PSS/n-Si.
watch_item: The abstract reports only 75-day ambient stability; longer-term durability and scalable, defect-free graphene integration remain unestablished.
paper_title: Synergistic Graphene and PEDOT:PSS Layers on Silicon for Enhanced Efficiency and Stability in Schottky Junction Solar Cells
